INFO-3-05.rationale: “Persistent pattern” and “measurably degrades” require the propagation thresholds and systemic impact metrics assigned to L8 in §§7 and 9, together with empirical attribution of degradation.

INFO-4-01.rationale: “Persistent I3 with measurable systemic impact” requires L8-calibrated tests, while §7's “escalates” supplies the I3-to-I4 relationship and the draft's additional exclusivity and mixed-content policies are not mandated.

INFO-5-01.rationale: “Determined exclusively by” followed by three sources does not settle whether all three are necessary for each determination or merely exhaust the permitted sources, separately from calibrating consensus thresholds.

INFO-5-02.rationale: “Truth SHALL NOT be determined by” clearly excludes the listed decision inputs, so tracing those inputs requires implementation records without a new normative rule.

INFO-5-03.rationale: “TTL expiry” has no defined relationship to the T₁/T₂ transitions or post-expiry state, requiring a temporal state model as well as calibrated durations.

INFO-6.1-01.rationale: “Time ≤ T₁” leaves the claim clock's starting event undefined and assigns T₁ to L8, although §5's “until PTL resolution” already allows resolved claims to leave I1.

INFO-6.1-02.rationale: “Downgraded to informational annotation” introduces an undefined state or representation outside I0–I4, while T₁ is explicitly an L8 parameter.

INFO-6.1-03.rationale: “I1 + time > T₂” requires a clock and a defined relationship between I1 and the earlier annotation downgrade, while threshold values and ordering belong to temporal calibration.

INFO-6.1-04.rationale: “MUST be calibrated under DKP-8-SIMULATION-001” explicitly assigns T₁ and T₂ to L8 and makes provenance validation depend on that referenced procedure.

INFO-6.2-01.rationale: “Unrelated system operations” and “non-dependent protocols” require operational dependency relationships that the upstream/downstream list in §2 does not fully define.

INFO-6.2-02.rationale: “Unless escalated by PTL-confirmed impact” supplies neither an escalation destination nor a transition model, while the impact metrics are assigned to L8 by §9.

INFO-7-01.rationale: “Escalates to Systemic Lie (I4) when” introduces conditions without settling whether every listed harm is required or alternative harms suffice, independently of the explicitly L8-calibrated thresholds.

INFO-7-02.rationale: “Measurable deviation from admissible system states” requires systemic impact metrics assigned to L8 by §9 and a definition or protocol mapping for admissible states that this document does not provide.

INFO-8-01.rationale: “MAY” makes the listed responses optional, and “annotations are informational disclosures, not enforcement actions” together with §9 resolves the draft's suggested annotation-versus-enforcement uncertainty.
INFO-8-01.rationale_reconciled: A MAY list of permitted responses; responses of other kinds are observable.

INFO-9-01.rationale: “Valid L8 Calibration Bundle” expressly requires propagation thresholds, temporal parameters, systemic impact metrics, confidence bounds, and validity windows whose calibration procedure is referenced externally.

INFO-9-02.rationale: “Absent a valid L8 bundle” requires calibration validity information, while §8 explicitly identifies annotations as informational disclosures, so their mandatory attachment does not establish the conflict proposed by the draft.

INFO-9-03.rationale: “Manual interpretation of truth status” concerns the protocol's truth-status processing under §5, and the draft's alternative ban on all human interpretation exceeds that scope and the exclusions in §0.

INFO-InformationalArbitration_Non-Remova.rationale: “The original claim remains visible and preserved” does not settle whether visibility must remain public or may be restricted to authorized viewers, which changes compliance with the non-removal obligation.

“Quantified probability of correspondence with physical reality” requires an empirical probability model, while “relevant oracle classes or node ranges” and the verification reference require PTL evidence.

“Shall not alter legal status, impose penalties, modify rights or obligations” states the prohibited effects clearly, but attributing observed downstream effects to annotations requires causal evidence.

“Isolated I3 events absent systemic impact” requires the propagation and impact tests assigned to L8 in §§7 and 9, while the accompanying bans on suppression and belief correction require implementation checks.

INTEGRATION-0-01.rationale: “Not compelled and not presumed” requires evidence about actual participation, while §§4–7 supply the phased controls and reversal requirements.

INTEGRATION-10-02.rationale: “MAY be audited under DKP-8-AUDIT-001” places audit procedure in an unavailable protocol, while “process integrity, not political preference” clearly states the permitted focus.

INTEGRATION-11-01.rationale: “Accelerated integration” does not distinguish prohibited procedural shortcuts from faster progression that still satisfies every phase validation.

INTEGRATION-11-03.rationale: “Retroactive enforcement” does not identify whether conduct, accrued obligations, or continuing legal status supplies the temporal reference for prohibited retroactivity.

INTEGRATION-11-04.rationale: “Bypass DKP-7-SCOPE-001” requires the scope restrictions contained in the referenced protocol, which is not supplied.

INTEGRATION-11-05.rationale: “Early phases” is contextualized by §4.3’s “until Full Integration,” and §10’s public documentation requirement supplies disclosure, so the draft overstates the remaining ambiguity.

INTEGRATION-12-01.rationale: “Controlled procedure of DKP-4-UPGRADE-001” delegates acceptance, activation, and rollback requirements to the referenced upgrade procedure and its simulation and audit dependencies.

INTEGRATION-12-02.rationale: “Recorded only by the ‘Last updated’ date” expressly resolves the treatment of presentation-only corrections, so the draft’s identifier ambiguity is not supported.

INTEGRATION-12-03.rationale: “Mandatory simulation under DKP-8-SIMULATION-001” requires the unavailable simulation rules, while “recorded only by the ‘Last updated’ date” resolves the presentation-only exception.

INTEGRATION-12-04.rationale: “DKP-4-UPGRADE-001 §3” is unavailable, but “do not change normative content” states the classification rule clearly, leaving semantic comparison to implementation and review.

INTEGRATION-2-01.rationale: “Force adoption of DKP” requires evidence of coercion and its attribution to protocol actions, rather than a choice between conflicting textual rules.

INTEGRATION-2-02.rationale: “Override existing legal systems during transition” prohibits what §9 potentially permits through “unless explicitly superseded,” without specifying how those rules interact.

INTEGRATION-2-03.rationale: “Impose cultural or ideological alignment” requires evidence about integration conditions and their coercive operation, without presenting competing permissions in the text.

INTEGRATION-3-03.rationale: “Without producing legal, economic, or administrative effects” leaves unresolved whether indirect consequences of observation count alongside direct system effects.

INTEGRATION-3-04.rationale: “PTL-anchored indicators” lacks a defined provenance relationship connecting derived compatibility indicators to PTL outputs.

INTEGRATION-3-05.rationale: “Measurable destabilization causally linked to DKP activation” requires measurements and a causal attribution model.

INTEGRATION-3-06.rationale: “Controlled reversion” is operationally constrained by declared scope and cost and §7’s continuity requirements, so unspecified additional controls do not establish a textual ambiguity.

INTEGRATION-4.1-01.rationale: “Explicit, auditable consent” and “Implicit or coerced consent is invalid” require authentic consent evidence and assessment of coercion.

INTEGRATION-4.3-01.rationale: “Fully reversible without punitive consequences” does not settle which real-world effects must be restored or distinguish prohibited punishment from the rollback costs expressly contemplated elsewhere.

INTEGRATION-5.1-01.rationale: “No legal, economic, or administrative effects” does not specify whether the prohibition includes indirect consequences of otherwise permitted read-only assessment.

INTEGRATION-5.1-02.rationale: “Valid consent declaration” inherits §4.1’s explicit, auditable, noncoerced consent requirements, whose substantive verification needs evidence about the consent process.

INTEGRATION-5.1-03.rationale: “Successful completion of data integrity and coverage checks” requires calibrated acceptance criteria, while “Voluntary withdrawal” requires evidence of the withdrawal decision.

INTEGRATION-5.2-01.rationale: “Advisory or opt-in mode” and “No sanctions, kill switches, or automatic enforcement” constrain module operation consistently with “fully sovereign,” so the draft identifies no necessary conflict.

INTEGRATION-5.2-02.rationale: “L8-simulated interface stability” explicitly assigns the missing stability model and acceptance calibration to L8.

INTEGRATION-5.2-03.rationale: “Verified operational stability within declared scope” needs calibrated stability limits and an observation period, supported by operational measurements.

INTEGRATION-5.3-02.rationale: “DKP-8-SIMULATION-001 stress-test clearance” delegates substantive clearance requirements to a protocol not supplied here.

INTEGRATION-5.3-03.rationale: “Rollback to Phase 1 if shock indicators appear” leaves its mandatory status unclear against §7’s “MAY be triggered,” while exit requirements depend on DKP-6-EXIT-001.

INTEGRATION-5.4-01.rationale: “Full rights and obligations” and “standard DKP-6-EXIT-001 rules” require the applicable protocols and exit specification absent from the supplied text.

INTEGRATION-5.4-02.rationale: “Long-term stability” and “Absence of unresolved systemic risk” require calibrated observation periods and acceptance criteria together with stability and risk evidence.

INTEGRATION-6-01.rationale: “Minimum biosphere and safety thresholds” requires calibration, while verification of “PTL data integrity and coverage,” manipulation, and capacity requires measurement evidence.

INTEGRATION-6-02.rationale: “Assessment relies exclusively on” restricts admissible evidence without independently mandating every category in every check, while “DKP-8-SIMULATION-001 stress testing” requires the referenced specification.

INTEGRATION-7-02.rationale: “Accelerated biospheric degradation” and “systemic unrest causally linked to protocol activation” require empirical detection and attribution, while “beyond modeled bounds” requires calibrated limits.

INTEGRATION-7-04.rationale: “Preserve data continuity and audit trails” supplies the preservation obligation, and implementing record inventories and continuity checks does not require an author-selected exception.

INTEGRATION-8-01.rationale: “Redistribute risk retroactively” and “expose current members to imported instability” require baseline and impact models, while “existing protocol guarantees” requires the relevant protocol content.

INTEGRATION-8-02.rationale: “Risk isolation and sandboxing” supplies no containment boundary or interface specification, and demonstrating effective isolation additionally requires risk evidence.

INTEGRATION-9-01.rationale: “Unless explicitly superseded” permits an exception during “all integration phases” whose relationship to §2’s prohibition on transition overrides is unresolved.

INTEGRATION-9-02.rationale: “Beyond interface compatibility” lacks a defined integration interface, while verifying that cultural and linguistic systems “remain untouched” requires evidence about integration effects.

INTEROP-1-01.rationale: The exclusions “harmonize legal systems,” “enforce DKP externally,” and “accept external norms as binding within DKP” specify prohibited effects; implementing their detection does not establish a competing normative reading.
INTEROP-1-01.rationale_reconciled: Three named exclusions of what INTEROP does (§1); a request for any of them is refused at the boundary, which is observable. 'Accept external norms as binding' is also checked under §5 (external rulings not binding).

INTEROP-10-01.rationale: “Automatic legal harmonization” is prohibited consistently with §1’s exclusion of harmonization and §3’s definition of translation as mapping representations.
INTEROP-10-01.rationale_reconciled: A prohibited pattern (§10); a harmonization performed by INTEROP is observable.

INTEROP-10-02.rationale: “Algorithmic dependency on external decision systems” does not distinguish prohibited reliance on their decisions from data or availability dependencies arising through the expressly permitted bridges and oracle mirroring.

INTEROP-10-03.rationale: “Governance-by-API” is distinguished from §7’s permitted “API access” by §1’s prohibition on implicit authority transfer and §4.3’s restriction on deriving legitimacy, obligation, or consent from compatibility.

INTEROP-10-04.rationale: “Silent import of external norms” is constrained by §3’s explicit-authorization condition, §5’s rejection of internally binding external rulings, and §11’s boundary-event recording requirement.

INTEROP-10-05.rationale: “Permanent delegation” does not settle whether an indefinite but revocable delegation is prohibited or whether permanence requires irrevocability.

INTEROP-11-01.rationale: The requirement “MUST be auditable” operates under the absent DKP-8-AUDIT-001, to which §11 exclusively assigns audit authority and §7 assigns audit-hook compatibility.

INTEROP-11-02.rationale: “MUST expose translation logic” does not specify whether access must be public or restricted to authorized auditors, and “open specifications” does not expressly settle access to the logic itself.

INTEROP-11-03.rationale: “MUST record boundary events for post-facto review” specifies the recording purpose, while a suitable event schema and storage policy are implementation work rather than unstated normative requirements.

INTEROP-11-04.rationale: “Governed exclusively by DKP-8-AUDIT-001” expressly places audit authority in a document outside the supplied corpus.

INTEROP-12-01.rationale: “Resolve geopolitical conflicts” clearly excludes a substantive conflict-resolution function from the protocol’s defined translational remit, leaving operation classification to implementation.
INTEROP-12-01.rationale_reconciled: A scope limitation (§12: SHALL NOT); a request is refused.

INTEROP-12-02.rationale: “Unify legal systems” is excluded consistently with §1’s rejection of legal harmonization and §3’s permitted mapping between distinct representations.
INTEROP-12-02.rationale_reconciled: A scope limitation (§12: SHALL NOT); a request is refused.

INTEROP-12-03.rationale: “Guarantee compliance by external actors” plainly restricts protocol commitments, so missing guarantee records or recognition code do not create a normative ambiguity.
INTEROP-12-03.rationale_reconciled: A scope limitation (§12: SHALL NOT); a guarantee of external compliance requested of INTEROP is refused; §5 leaves compliance to Subjects.

INTEROP-12-04.rationale: “Act as an enforcement bridge” is bounded in both directions by §1’s exclusion of enforcing DKP externally and §5’s refusal to recognize external rulings as internally binding.
INTEROP-12-04.rationale_reconciled: A scope limitation (§12: SHALL NOT); acting as an enforcement bridge is refused; directives to external systems are also checked under §3 (INTEROP-3-01).

INTEROP-12-05.rationale: “Compatibility, not convergence” summarizes the defined translational interfaces and exclusions of legal harmonization and unification, so the draft’s demand for an additional independent acceptance standard is unsupported.
INTEROP-12-05.rationale_reconciled: Read as a conjunction fixed by the rest of the text: compatibility = every interaction through a defined interface and translation (§3, §4.4); no convergence = no harmonization or unification (§1, §10, §12) and no external norm adopted (§5, §10). Both parts are observable; the draft 'checkable: no' is corrected to partial.

INTEROP-13-01.rationale: “The controlled procedure of DKP-4-UPGRADE-001” expressly delegates the upgrade process, including its simulation, audit, activation, and rollback requirements, to absent protocols.

INTEROP-13-02.rationale: “Any modification requires a new protocol identifier” is qualified by presentation-only corrections being “recorded only” through the date, while the draft supplies no textual basis for competing identifier-freshness regimes.

INTEROP-13-03.rationale: “Mandatory simulation under DKP-8-SIMULATION-001” requires the simulation procedure specified by an absent document.

INTEROP-13-05.rationale: Corrections that “do not change normative content” receive date-only correction recording, while “each published edition” separately requires an integrity digest, so these clauses do not establish the draft’s claimed recording conflict.

INTEROP-13-06.rationale: The “canonical source” and its listing in “SHA256SUMS.txt” must be obtained from the named canonical repository; the text specifies SHA-256 and does not require an additional canonicalization transformation.

INTEROP-2-01.rationale: “Purely translational” is explained by §3’s “deterministic mapping between DKP-native representations and external representations” and the authority restrictions in §4.
INTEROP-2-01.rationale_reconciled: 'Purely translational' is concretized by §§3-5 and §9-10: INTEROP records, translates and exports as evidence; it performs no action of its own. An INTEROP action is observable.

INTEROP-3-02.rationale: “A formally defined interface” requires an interface specification but does not require the protocol author to select its specification language.
INTEROP-3-02.rationale_reconciled: The definition requires a formally defined interface at every interaction; whether a boundary record names a declared interface is observable. The formal specification of each interface is not given in the text and is a lab list.

INTEROP-3-03.rationale: “Deterministic mapping” supplies the required property, while declaring each integration’s representations, inputs, and contextual state belongs to implementing that mapping.
INTEROP-3-03.rationale_reconciled: 'Deterministic mapping' is checkable as: the same external input gives the same translation (across runs and against the declared mapping). The content of the mapping for values is open under §6 (INTEROP-6-02, UNKNOWN); determinism is not.

INTEROP-3-04.rationale: “Implicit import of external authority, norms, or obligations” and “without explicit protocol authorization” already define the classification conditions; the missing import and authorization checks are implementation work.
INTEROP-3-04.rationale_reconciled: Normative leakage is defined by its effects (external authority, norms or obligations entering DKP without protocol authorization); §5 and §10 name the forms: executing an external ruling, compliance acts by the system, a silent norm import. Each is an observable event.

INTEROP-4.1-01.rationale: Checking whether an operation would “override or reinterpret DKP axioms” requires the absent DKP-1-AXIOMS-001 named in §2.

INTEROP-4.2-01.rationale: “Beyond DKP-7-SCOPE-001” explicitly delegates the jurisdictional boundary to a document outside the supplied corpus.

INTEROP-4.3-01.rationale: “SHALL NOT be treated as legitimacy, obligation, or consent” clearly prohibits the inference, while representations of those statuses and inference records remain implementation choices.
INTEROP-4.3-01.rationale_reconciled: A recorded inference of consent, legitimacy or obligation from compatibility is observable; implicit treatment without a record is not, so the check is partial.

INTEROP-4.4-01.rationale: Assessing “auditable translation rules” depends on the audit framework referenced by §7’s “audit hooks compatible with DKP-8-AUDIT-001” and §11’s exclusive assignment of audit authority.

INTEROP-5-04.rationale: “Does not adjudicate conflicts between external legal regimes” prohibits deciding those conflicts, while §5 expressly permits exporting “evidence, signals, or reference data.”
INTEROP-5-04.rationale_reconciled: A clear exclusion: DKP gives no ruling between external regimes. A request for such a ruling is refused.

INTEROP-6-02.rationale: “Justice-weighted internal equivalents” supplies neither the internal value representation nor the conversion relation, while the justice weights themselves require calibration.

INTEROP-6-03.rationale: “Full externality internalization” requires an empirical accounting model and evidence identifying, attributing, and valuing the externalities to be internalized.

INTEROP-6-05.rationale: “DKP-2-FINANCE-001 constraints” explicitly requires constraints from a document outside the supplied corpus.

INTEROP-7-01.rationale: “Open specifications” does not settle whether public readability suffices or whether licensing and unrestricted implementation rights are also required.

INTEROP-7-02.rationale: “Cryptographic verifiability” leaves the verified artifacts, asserted properties, and trust relationships undefined, so a verification contract is missing.

INTEROP-7-03.rationale: “Audit hooks compatible with DKP-8-AUDIT-001” requires the interface requirements of the absent audit protocol.

INTEROP-7-04.rationale: “Black-box or proprietary” makes either classification sufficient to prohibit authoritative trust, leaving classification evidence and enforcement checks to implementation.

INTEROP-8-01.rationale: “Only as” introduces “untrusted inputs” and “I1 (Unverified Claims)” without stating whether every untrusted input must also receive I1 classification, whose governing DKP-5-INFO-001 is absent.

INTEROP-8-02.rationale: “PTL verification” names a verification mechanism without defining PTL, its interface, or the evidence establishing that verification occurred.

INTEROP-9-01.rationale: “The interop boundary MUST degrade gracefully” lacks defined degraded boundary states and transitions, although the adjacent clauses constrain internal effects and rollback.

INTEROP-9-02.rationale: “DKP internal execution MUST remain unaffected” does not settle whether preservation concerns logical execution and state or also timing and availability, producing different compliance results.

INTEROP-9-03.rationale: “No rollback of DKP state is permitted” sits within §9’s explicit failure conditional, while §13 separately governs upgrade rollback, so the draft’s unrestricted rollback prohibition is unsupported.

INTSEC-1-01.rationale: The exclusion of “surveillance” and “profiling” does not establish where permitted “evidence collection and heightened verification” cross into those excluded functions.

INTSEC-10-01.rationale: “Interfaces with” lists module responsibilities such as “freeze / restore semantics” without defining the messages, directionality, or contracts connecting those external protocols.

INTSEC-11-01.rationale: “No PTL evidence → no coercive action” states a clear necessary condition, with §4.4’s evidence traceability supplying the association requirement and PTL supplying external validation.

INTSEC-11-02.rationale: “Minimal sufficient containment” requires an action-effect model to establish sufficiency and calibrated comparisons of scope, duration, and integrity loss to evaluate minimality.

INTSEC-11-03.rationale: “Complete audit trail” is operationalized by §4.4’s logging and evidence traceability for “all actions” and §5’s auditable transitions, without requiring the draft’s unspecified additional event population.

INTSEC-11-04.rationale: “Preference for reversibility” requires calibrated action-selection weights or ordering informed by reversal feasibility, subject to §4.4’s explicit reversal and irreversible-authorization constraints.

INTSEC-11-05.rationale: “No cross-layer authority overreach” combines §2’s explicit L3 restrictions with authority rules belonging to the other named layer protocols.

INTSEC-12-01.rationale: “Controlled procedure of DKP-4-UPGRADE-001” and the named simulation and audit protocols expressly delegate acceptance, activation, and rollback requirements to external documents.

INTSEC-12-02.rationale: “A new protocol identifier,” qualified by the explicit “Presentation-only corrections” exception, supplies the rule without establishing the draft’s additional corpus-wide novelty test.

INTSEC-12-03.rationale: “Explicit incompatibility declaration” requires an express declaration, while a prescribed format or enumeration of compatibility boundaries is an additional obligation invented by the draft.

INTSEC-12-04.rationale: “DKP-8-SIMULATION” is an unresolved document identifier whose mapping to “DKP-8-SIMULATION-001” is not declared, and simulation coverage depends on the referenced specification.

INTSEC-12-05.rationale: “DKP-4-UPGRADE-001 §3” supplies the external exception definition, while “recorded only” governs correction metadata and the separate “each published edition” digest requirement remains explicit.

INTSEC-2-01.rationale: “Downstream,” “upstream,” and “in coordination with” name architectural relationships without defining their dataflow, execution-order, or interface obligations.

INTSEC-2-02.rationale: “Compute Justice outcomes,” “revoke rights or privileges autonomously,” and “introduce punishment logic” clearly prohibit those operations, leaving executable-operation checks and the externally governed “axiomatic constraints” to supply.

INTSEC-2-03.rationale: “Formal input triggers submitted to DKP-1-JUSTICE-001 or DKP-1-IDENTITY-001” requires an unspecified cross-protocol trigger contract, although “never by direct execution at L3” settles the authority restriction.

INTSEC-3.1-01.rationale: “Any detectable deviation between” the three state representations requires a common comparison model that is absent, but does not require the draft’s additional reading that all three must disagree.

INTSEC-3.2-01.rationale: “Produces or imminently enables an Integrity Violation” requires causal evidence and an enablement model, with imminence requiring calibration constrained by the ban on speculative triggers.

INTSEC-3.2-02.rationale: “Intent, ideology, affiliation, or declared motivation SHALL NOT be considered” fixes the exclusion, while detecting direct or indirect decision dependencies is a verification implementation task.

INTSEC-3.3-01.rationale: “Cryptographically verifiable commitments anchored to the Physical Truth Layer and ultimately to Genesis Block #0” depends on external trust anchors and an unspecified commitment and anchoring-chain representation.

INTSEC-3.3-02.rationale: “DTI-Day (DKP-0-TIME-001)” and “Proof-of-Synergy consensus rules” require external specifications, while “immune to discretionary suppression” additionally needs an availability and adversary model.

INTSEC-4.1-01.rationale: “May only respond to PTL-confirmed states or PTL-confirmed divergence” and “may [not] redefine or override” establish clear checks whose implementation needs action provenance and external PTL confirmation validation.

INTSEC-4.2-01.rationale: The draft’s uncertainty about “PTL-evidenced” is resolved by §4.1’s restriction on all security actions and §11’s “No PTL evidence → no coercive action,” leaving trigger checks and governing authorization rules.

INTSEC-4.3-01.rationale: “Strictly proportional,” “limited in scope and duration,” and “sufficient only to stop ongoing or imminent damage” require calibrated containment criteria supported by integrity-loss measurements and action-effect models.

INTSEC-4.3-02.rationale: “Escalation to higher layers” lacks a receiving-layer and handoff definition, while “expansive” leaves the scope of actions requiring that escalation unsettled.

INTSEC-4.4-01.rationale: “Reversible where physically and logically possible” requires action-specific feasibility evidence, while “logged immutably” and “traceable to triggering evidence” require implemented audit checks.

INTSEC-4.4-02.rationale: “Elevated authorization thresholds” requires calibrated authorization levels, whereas “and justification” clearly requires a justification without prescribing the draft’s additional sufficiency standard.

INTSEC-5-01.rationale: “Finite-state system” lists S0–S4 without complete entry predicates or a transition graph, and “governed by Dikenocratic Time” delegates clock semantics to DKP-0-TIME-001.

INTSEC-5-02.rationale: “Heightened verification” needs a calibrated increase over normal verification, while “7 DTI-Days” fixes the duration and the general “unless escalated” clause already applies to S1.

INTSEC-5-03.rationale: “Maximum duration: 14 DTI-Days unless escalated” fixes the ordinary timeout but does not define the state or deadline lifecycle after escalation.

INTSEC-5-04.rationale: The general “unless escalated” clause applies to S3’s “3 DTI-Days,” but the resulting escalated state and timeout handling remain structurally undefined.

INTSEC-5-06.rationale: “Automatically reverted to S0 upon expiration of the maximum duration unless escalated” specifies ordinary expiry but supplies no transition or timer behavior for escalated episodes.

INTSEC-6-01.rationale: “Triggers (PTL-Anchored)” and §4.1’s “only respond to PTL-confirmed states” settle the Justice trigger’s evidence requirement, leaving classifiers and external authorization rules to implement.

INTSEC-6-02.rationale: “Handled exclusively by DKP-0-ORACLE-001” expressly delegates PTL divergence and oracle inconsistency handling to the unavailable Oracle protocol.

INTSEC-6-03.rationale: “Immediately suspend and defer to L0 resolution” requires a halt-event and resumption state machine, but does not itself license the draft’s proposed nonzero delay allowance.

INTSEC-7.1-01.rationale: “Mandatory transaction multi-signature requirement” lacks a signer and quorum contract and “sensitive or high-impact” needs calibration, while “Permitted actions” already permits imposing that requirement.

INTSEC-7.1-02.rationale: “Artificial throttling” and “economic slowdown” require performance baselines and causal attribution of action effects, with measurement tolerances requiring calibration.

INTSEC-7.2-01.rationale: “Temporary freeze of disputed transactions or assets” lacks a dispute-status and freeze-termination lifecycle, whose execution must also conform to the named Identity, Justice, Finance, and Assets interfaces.

INTSEC-7.3-01.rationale: “Forced safe-mode execution” and “multi-party authorization” lack behavioral and participant contracts, whereas their placement under “Permitted actions” settles permission to impose these measures.

INTSEC-7.4-01.rationale: “Non-essential execution paths” requires an essentiality map, and “request for PTL systemic halt where applicable” requires applicability and request contracts with Oracle.

INTSEC-8-01.rationale: “Mass surveillance” leaves its boundary with permitted evidence collection unspecified, although “without PTL trigger” supplies no affirmative permission to override §1’s surveillance exclusion.

INTSEC-8-02.rationale: “Collective punishment or guilt by association,” reinforced by §2’s ban on “punishment logic,” establishes a clear prohibition whose attribution and decision-ground checks remain to implement.

INTSEC-8-03.rationale: “Permanent exclusion without Justice-domain outcome” delegates the relevant outcome to Justice, and §2’s exclusive formal-trigger route prevents treating an unrelated outcome as independent L3 authorization.

INTSEC-8-04.rationale: “Secrecy of rules or hidden enforcement logic” does not settle whether disclosure to auditors, affected Subjects, or everyone is required.

INTSEC-8-05.rationale: “Justified by ideology or narrative” concerns the grounds for action, and the exclusive PTL-evidence requirements distinguish those grounds from ordinary textual descriptions of admissible evidence.

INTSEC-8-06.rationale: “As defined by oracle and control concentration limits in DKP-0-ORACLE-001” expressly delegates control and aggregation definitions, while “4%” already fixes the numeric limit.

INTSEC-8-07.rationale: “Violation constitutes a critical architectural breach” immediately follows the standalone 4% control prohibition, providing its antecedent without the draft’s unsupported extension to every section 8 ban.

INTSEC-9-01.rationale: “Reversal and appeal conditions under Justice protocol” requires the external Justice rules, while “MUST explicitly define” makes the remaining disclosure checks straightforward to implement.

JUSTICE-1-01.rationale: “Binding justice outputs” requires a downstream enforcement contract that this document does not define, although §§7–9 explain the preventive purpose of non-punitive consequences.

JUSTICE-10-01.rationale: “Distributed proportionally to responsibility weights” and “exceeding its attributable contribution” require an undefined allocation and comparison structure for heterogeneous consequence-vector components.

JUSTICE-10-02.rationale: “Collective responsibility SHALL NOT nullify individual accountability,” read with §10's per-Subject allocations and §12's no-exemption rule, requires preserving individual obligations without a new normative definition.
JUSTICE-10-02.rationale_reconciled: With a collective among the responsible Subjects, every individual Subject with an attributable contribution keeps its own share; a share absorbed by the collective is observable.

JUSTICE-11-01.rationale: “SHALL be re-evaluated when” leaves response timing to operational calibration under the temporal rules, while detecting that “system boundary conditions shift” requires observations.

JUSTICE-11-02.rationale: “Minimum TTL” requires temporal provenance metadata, but §3's listed inputs provide no TTL interface and §2 prohibits direct access to the underlying Physical Truth Layer data.

JUSTICE-11-03.rationale: “Incomplete, stale, or selectively withheld data” requires expected-evidence, freshness, and disclosure information that cannot be established from submitted values alone.

JUSTICE-11-04.rationale: “Oscillatory relief, temporary concealment, or strategic delay of mitigation” requires longitudinal behavioural evidence and a detection model with calibrated observation windows.

JUSTICE-12-01.rationale: “No Subject SHALL be exempt” on the five listed grounds is a clear decision-rule constraint, while detecting hidden reliance on those grounds requires evidence rather than author clarification.
JUSTICE-12-01.rationale_reconciled: No exemption by status, authority, jurisdiction, ideology or culture: a declared status must not change the outcome. Checked metamorphically (the same run without the status gives the same shares and domains).

JUSTICE-13-01.rationale: “Reinterpret impact metrics,” “alter identity attribution,” “override axiom-defined bounds,” and “inject policy, governance, or moral reasoning” explicitly constrain implementation, with authoritative input meanings supplied by the referenced protocols.
JUSTICE-13-01.rationale_reconciled: Four isolation bans: impact metrics and identity attribution used as given (flag and weights unchanged), no policy, governance or moral field in the output. Axiom-defined bounds are modelled only as the declared safe margin (partial).

JUSTICE-14-01.rationale: “Deterministic,” “reproducible,” “fully auditable,” and “traceable to protocol inputs” specify the required properties, leaving replay environments and audit evidence to implementation without demonstrating conflicting readings.
JUSTICE-14-01.rationale_reconciled: 'Opaque, discretionary or non-reproducible' is checkable: every decision is recomputed from its IMPACT and IDENTITY inputs by the §6-§9 rules, and re-execution gives the same log.

JUSTICE-15-01.rationale: “Controlled procedure of DKP-4-UPGRADE-001” expressly delegates acceptance, activation, and rollback requirements to a document absent from the supplied corpus.

JUSTICE-15-02.rationale: “Full-system simulation under DKP-8-SIMULATION” depends on the simulation specification, whose full identifier “DKP-8-SIMULATION-001” is supplied earlier in the same section.

JUSTICE-15-03.rationale: “Recorded only by the ‘Last updated’ date” does not settle whether additional correction logs are forbidden or merely excluded from protocol version identification, and the cited upgrade exception is external.

JUSTICE-15-04.rationale: “Canonical source of each published edition” and “SHA256SUMS.txt” require the source files, edition records, and manifest from the explicitly named canonical repository.

JUSTICE-2-01.rationale: “Above” and “below all economic, governance, security, and enforcement protocols” require an architectural relation and protocol mapping beyond the input dependencies specified in §2.

JUSTICE-3.3-01.rationale: §3.3 imports constraints “From DKP-1-AXIOMS-001,” while §2 requires “All inputs” to come “exclusively” from Impact and Identity, leaving their permitted import route unresolved.

JUSTICE-4-01.rationale: “Consequence Vector C” lacks a component schema and structural mapping from the three input classes, separate from calibration of consequence values.

JUSTICE-4-02.rationale: “Moral language,” “intent interpretation,” “discretionary adjustment,” and “subjective weighting” explicitly prohibit content and computation practices; needing checks for them does not establish competing normative readings.
JUSTICE-4-02.rationale_reconciled: Four exclusions from the output vector C; a field carrying a moral assessment, an intent reading, a discretionary adjustment or a subjective weight is observable on the recorded vector.

JUSTICE-5-01.rationale: “Evaluated independently” and “No domain SHALL be skipped” require separate domain evaluations, while §9 expressly references mitigation and isolation failure and therefore rules out the draft's proposed total absence of computational dependence.
JUSTICE-5-01.rationale_reconciled: 'Evaluated independently' is checkable as: each domain's result equals what its own §6-§9 conditions give, so no domain's result depends on another's. The conditions themselves are checked under §6-§9 (restriction margins are declared).

JUSTICE-6-01.rationale: “Mitigation or repair is physically possible” requires physical feasibility evidence, whereas “Rᵢ = True” explicitly states the required reversibility flag value.

JUSTICE-6-02.rationale: “Required mitigation scope,” “proportional restitution obligations,” and “time constraints” require a calibrated restitution model and deadlines informed by repair feasibility.

JUSTICE-6-03.rationale: “Restitution SHALL NOT exceed the measurable impact” requires an undefined comparison mapping between restitution obligations and the “channel-separated, unaggregated” impact quantities.

JUSTICE-7-01.rationale: “Safe margins” and “repeated harmful behavior” need calibrated thresholds or observation windows, while “mitigation capacity is insufficient” needs an empirical capacity assessment.

JUSTICE-7-02.rationale: “Proportional” and “continuously re-evaluated” require a calibrated consequence model and review cadence under §11, while “where physically possible” requires feasibility evidence.

JUSTICE-7-03.rationale: “SHALL exist solely to prevent further harm” supplies the governing purpose, but establishing whether a restriction actually serves that purpose requires causal and use evidence.

JUSTICE-8-01.rationale: “Subject behavior presents systemic risk” requires a behavioural risk model and calibration, while “Rᵢ = False” and “Xᵢ = True” explicitly identify the other trigger values.

JUSTICE-8-02.rationale: “Minimal in scope” requires a calibrated scope comparison model, and “targeted strictly at harm prevention” requires evidence about the effectiveness of feasible alternatives.

JUSTICE-8-03.rationale: “Prioritize functional separation over physical confinement whenever technically feasible” establishes the preference, leaving feasibility and sufficiency to empirical assessment without requiring the draft's suggested failed trials.

JUSTICE-9-01.rationale: “Fail to contain harm” and “refuses or is incapable of compliance” require outcome and behavioural evidence, while “persistently” requires a calibrated persistence rule.

JUSTICE-9-03.rationale: “Conditions leading to loss of life” requires a causal survival model, and consistency with “Axiom A1” additionally depends on the referenced DKP-1-AXIOMS-001.

JUSTICE-9-04.rationale: “Indirect lethal exposure” and “abandonment” require evidence about exclusion's effects and continued support, while “system-provided privileges only” already specifies the permitted authority.

JUSTICE-DisputeExceptionClause-01.rationale: “Scheduled periodic re-evaluation cycles only” and “SHALL NOT be rejected solely on TTL grounds” settle the TTL rule, while qualifying admissibility is delegated to DKP-1-EPISTEMIC-BOUNDARIES-001 §7.1.

JUSTICE-DisputeExceptionClause-02.rationale: “A valid Dispute Event” followed by “provided” and conditions a)–c) states cumulative requirements within externally defined dispute procedures, so the draft's proposed self-contained, exhaustive validity definition is unsupported.

LABOR-1-01.rationale: “Forced into labor to preserve life” requires evidence about survival needs and actual compulsion, while §4.1 expressly prohibits making baseline access contingent on labor.

LABOR-10-01.rationale: “Under Restriction or Isolation per DKP-1-JUSTICE-001” delegates the governing justice states and applicable restrictions to an unsupplied protocol.

LABOR-10-02.rationale: “Retain pathways for justice recovery” requires evidence that pathways remain accessible and effective under the justice states supplied by DKP-1-JUSTICE-001.

LABOR-10-03.rationale: “Participation remains voluntary outside crisis conditions” expressly qualifies voluntariness and connects to §9.2, so the draft's additional unresolved crisis-exception reading is unnecessary.

LABOR-11-01.rationale: “Directly bindable” requires binding capability, reinforced by §3.3's record “linking” a Subject, while identity details come from DKP-1-IDENTITY-001 rather than an invented requirement for a publicly materialized identity link.

LABOR-11-02.rationale: “Proxy, fictitious, or obscured participation” requires verification of actual actors and activities against the identity binding and measured-impact evidence required by §11.

LABOR-12-01.rationale: “Redefine justice logic” and “override impact measurements” require authoritative upstream references, while “function as punishment or discipline” requires evidence of actual operation.

LABOR-13-01.rationale: “Through the controlled procedure of DKP-4-UPGRADE-001” delegates sequencing, acceptance, and “rollback” requirements to that protocol and its referenced simulation and audit procedures.

LABOR-13-02.rationale: “Presentation-only corrections that do not change normative content are not Upgrades” and “recorded only” expressly supply the exception to “Any modification,” while simulation execution depends on the referenced protocol.

LABOR-13-03.rationale: “Do not change normative content” states the equivalence condition, and “Last updated” plainly identifies the document's last_updated metadata field, leaving comparison and recording to implementation.

LABOR-2-01.rationale: “Strictly downstream,” “above,” “alongside,” and “below” name relationships without defining their operational dependency or precedence semantics.

LABOR-3.1-01.rationale: “Contributes to restoration, maintenance, or protection” and “causally attributed to a Subject” require empirical models, while “sustained” requires a calibrated duration criterion.

LABOR-3.2-01.rationale: “Recognized labor or restorative activity” leaves the recognition mechanism and representation of restorative eligibility unspecified, while “voluntary engagement” requires supporting evidence.

LABOR-4.1-01.rationale: “Minimum life-preserving resources” requires measured needs and adequacy models, with additional requirements delegated to the unsupplied “Axiom A1.”

LABOR-4.2-02.rationale: “Full participation and access” lacks a defined rights-and-access state mapping, while the amount of “measurable contribution or restitution” needed for recovery requires calibration.

LABOR-5.1-01.rationale: “Enabling recovery,” “non-humiliating,” and “scaled to Subject capacity and context” require effectiveness and experience assessments plus calibrated capacity scaling.

LABOR-5.1-02.rationale: “Preventing exploitation, monoculture, or forced specialization” requires causal and detection models, while adequacy of “plural and diverse” opportunities requires calibrated measures.

LABOR-5.2-01.rationale: “A deterministic function” leaves the recovery model to calibration, while “relevance to harmed impact channels” additionally lacks a defined mapping between contributions and harmed channels.

LABOR-5.2-02.rationale: “Symbolic, performative, or purely declarative activity SHALL NOT be recognized as labor” supplies an explicit exclusion, so the draft invents an unresolved precedence question against the general labor definition.

LABOR-6-01.rationale: “Debt bondage,” “open-ended obligation,” and required “alignment” require evidence about actual labor conditions, while §9.2 expressly provides the bounded crisis exception to voluntary participation.

LABOR-7-01.rationale: “System needs derived from impact deficits” and “avoidance of concentration, exploitation, or dependency” require needs and outcome models with calibrated allocation criteria.

LABOR-7-02.rationale: “No centralized authority MAY monopolize assignment” requires an authority-and-control model defining the assignment domain over which monopoly is assessed.

LABOR-7-03.rationale: “Transparent, auditable, and rule-based” requires an allocation disclosure and audit interface whose audience, accessible rules, and evidence contract are not specified.

LABOR-8.1-02.rationale: “Proportional to measured impact” requires calibrated conversion parameters and a common representation for the listed compensation forms, rather than treating a missing coefficient as textual ambiguity.

LABOR-8.2-01.rationale: “Measurable stabilizing impact” and “appropriate physical or informational proxies” require empirical validation under the referenced but unsupplied DKP-1-IMPACT-001.

LABOR-9.1-02.rationale: “Outside formally declared crisis conditions” precedes a separate refusal list without expressly settling whether “does not constitute a violation” and “does not trigger punishment” survive crisis modulation, although §4.1 independently protects baseline access.

LABOR-9.2-01.rationale: “Formally declared crisis under DKP-4-CRISIS-001” depends on an unsupplied protocol, while “failure of participation would threaten systemic survival or collapse” requires a counterfactual model.

LABOR-9.2-02.rationale: “Strictly time-limited” and “proportionate to the declared threat” require calibrated bounds and models, while “preserve Axiom A1” and “prioritize Axiom A2” depend on the referenced axioms.

ORACLE-1-01.rationale: The 'sole admissible interface' requirement lacks a defined governance-system boundary and interface map identifying all physical-reality input paths.

ORACLE-1-02.rationale: 'Physical state only' is elaborated by §§4–5 and the explicit prohibited operations; missing executable content checks do not establish competing normative readings.

ORACLE-10-01.rationale: 'Likelihood updates' and 'long-term reliability' require statistical models and reliability data, while 'posterior distributions define S(t)' lacks a posterior-to-vector mapping.

ORACLE-10-02.rationale: 'Deterministic Bayesian ensemble' and 'Given identical inputs' require reproducible aggregation results; the draft's bitwise-serialization requirement is not stated.

ORACLE-10-03.rationale: 'Auditable and explainable' supplies no acceptance standard, allowing materially different judgments about whether a pipeline satisfies the requirement.

ORACLE-11-01.rationale: 'Posterior distributions ... differ by more than 7%' lacks a distribution-distance operator, percentage basis, and multi-class comparison rule.

ORACLE-11-02.rationale: 'A divergence flag is emitted' and 'all dependent state-based transactions SHALL be frozen' directly specify actions to apply using the implementation's transaction dependencies.

ORACLE-11-03.rationale: 'Maximum arbitration window: 14 days' fixes the duration but leaves the arbitration lifecycle's start event and unresolved-expiry transition undefined.

ORACLE-11-04.rationale: 'Convergence within the threshold, or exclusion of faulty or compromised sources' explicitly states alternatives, so the draft invents an additional convergence requirement after exclusion.

ORACLE-12-01.rationale: 'Immutable outputs' is expressly qualified by permitted 'measurement error correction under DKP-4-ERROR-001,' whose correction mechanics are not supplied.

ORACLE-12-02.rationale: 'Confidence envelope for each output ∈ [0,1]' supplies bounds but no data type or structure for the envelope.

ORACLE-12-03.rationale: 'Composite physical index' requires the B(t) model that the following paragraph explicitly assigns to DKP-8-SIMULATION-001.

ORACLE-12-05.rationale: 'Raw, model-declared output' must be obtained from the B(t) model explicitly assigned to L8; the prohibition on subsequent PTL alteration is clear.

ORACLE-12-06.rationale: 'An attached and valid L8 calibration bundle' requires an undefined bundle-attachment and validity contract in addition to the L8 calibration itself.

ORACLE-13-01.rationale: 'Aggregate confidence' and 'systemic oracle integrity is compromised' lack aggregation and integrity predicates, although §16 supplies the numeric confidence and coverage thresholds.

ORACLE-13-02.rationale: 'Blocks execution of L2 and higher layers' and 'preserves identity attribution, impact records, and subject continuity' define preservation checks; missing halt-trigger computation concerns a different provision.

ORACLE-14-01.rationale: 'Formally activated under Appendix A.4' requires the external activation rules, while 'caused by non-anthropogenic global physical events' requires causal evidence.

ORACLE-14-02.rationale: 'Events resulting from human action' requires causal attribution evidence and states no exemption for events that also have natural causes.

ORACLE-14-03.rationale: 'DOES NOT modify TTL values,' 'DOES NOT restore stale data weights,' and 'DOES NOT alter aggregation logic' specify direct configuration and state-invariant checks.

ORACLE-14-04.rationale: 'In accordance with Appendix A.4' and 'see DKP-7-SCOPE-001' explicitly place the duration and authority constraints in referenced documents not supplied.

ORACLE-15-01.rationale: 'No higher-layer protocol may' perform the five listed interactions gives explicit prohibitions; missing interaction tracing and enforcement checks are implementation gaps.

ORACLE-16-01.rationale: '4%,' '4%,' and '7%' explicitly fix the three constants, leaving only configuration checks to implement.

ORACLE-16-02.rationale: '14 days,' '< 60%,' and '80%' explicitly provide the arbitration limit and halt settings, including §13's minimum coverage threshold.

ORACLE-18-02.rationale: 'Re-anchoring assessment against Genesis Block #0' requires the referenced Genesis anchors to assess substantive compatibility.

ORACLE-2-01.rationale: 'Compatibility with Genesis Block physical anchors and parameters' requires the referenced Genesis Block values and constraints, which are not supplied.

ORACLE-2-02.rationale: 'Under explicitly defined activation and scope rules' requires a cross-layer consumption contract that this document neither defines nor maps to specific rules.

ORACLE-3-01.rationale: 'Human testimony or manual input' does not settle whether the exclusion covers administrative registration and configuration as well as measurement inputs.

ORACLE-4.1-01.rationale: 'Physically measurable variables' requires measurement procedures and evidence establishing measurability for the actual variables selected.

ORACLE-4.2-01.rationale: 'Hardware-bound' and 'traceable to a registered oracle identity' require an attestation and registry trust model that the document does not define.

ORACLE-4.3-01.rationale: 'Controlling one or more oracle sources' leaves indirect and shared control unresolved, affecting whose sources are combined under the owner cap.

ORACLE-4.4-01.rationale: 'A normalized reliability contribution' lacks a normalization domain and a rule relating normalization to capping and forced zero weights.

ORACLE-4.5-01.rationale: 'The fraction of the target physical domain' lacks a defined domain and measure, while 'actively observed' additionally requires observation-footprint evidence.

ORACLE-4.7-01.rationale: 'Physical separation of sensing mechanisms' can denote spatial or measurement-principle separation, and §6's platform categories do not settle that distinction.

ORACLE-4.8-01.rationale: 'Statistically significant disagreement' is not explicitly equated with §11's 'more than 7%' trigger, leaving an additional significance requirement unresolved.

ORACLE-5.1-01.rationale: 'Directly observable quantities' requires examination of the actual measurement method to establish whether it observes a quantity directly or derives a proxy.

ORACLE-5.2-01.rationale: 'Correlating with physical processes' requires empirical validation of the proxy relationship; the draft's demand for a particular correlation strength is not stated.

ORACLE-5.2-02.rationale: 'Include propagated uncertainty' requires the declared proxy model and its input-error model to verify propagation, although the declaration requirements are explicit.

ORACLE-5.3-01.rationale: 'SHALL NOT emit outputs concerning' explicitly enumerates the excluded domains, including consent; missing output labels and the draft's PPDI reference introduce no textual ambiguity.

ORACLE-6-01.rationale: 'Fixed terrestrial or marine sensors' overlaps with 'mobile or robotic sensing platforms' for fixed robotic sensors, without an assignment rule.

ORACLE-7-01.rationale: 'Cryptographically signed at the source,' 'a verifiable clock,' and registered-identity traceability specify required properties without requiring a unique cryptographic implementation.

ORACLE-7-02.rationale: 'Open' and 'proprietary' lack criteria distinguishing publicly documented but proprietary formats, whose acceptance cannot be decided by public decodability alone.

ORACLE-7-03.rationale: 'At ingestion time' requires a pipeline-stage boundary separating validation and decoding from the aggregation expressly required by §10.

ORACLE-8-02.rationale: 'Slashing of the violating owner’s remaining stake, where applicable' leaves total versus partial forfeiture unresolved and supplies no staking-applicability contract.

ORACLE-9-01.rationale: 'All data types SHALL have an explicit TTL' and 'exceeding its TTL' directly specify the registry-presence and strict age-comparison checks.

ORACLE-9-02.rationale: 'Stale data MUST NOT be' extrapolated, interpolated, substituted, or averaged prohibits stale-data use, not independently admitting a fresh observation as the draft suggests.

ORACLE-9-03.rationale: 'Explicit uncertainty, degradation, or halt signals' expressly permits alternatives and forbids neutral-state substitution; the draft invents a requirement for one prescribed signal per condition.

ORACLE-EpistemicInterpretationNote-01.rationale: 'Measurement records of physical states at specific times' requires a recoverable state-time association but does not mandate a field rather than provenance representation.

ORACLE-EpistemicInterpretationNote-02.rationale: 'Higher layers overriding measured reality' is prohibited, while the same note explicitly delegates legitimate measurement-error correction to DKP-4-ERROR-001.

ORACLE-EpistemicInterpretationNote-03.rationale: 'Measurement error correction under DKP-4-ERROR-001' requires the missing correction protocol, while the denial of 'permanent validity beyond defined TTL windows' is explicit.

POLICE-0-01.rationale: “The sole function” establishes a closed list of permitted functions, so mixed purposes require checking against that list rather than the additional normative rule invented by the draft.
POLICE-0-01.rationale_reconciled: 'The sole function' lists four functions; §3 (MAY list) and §4 (triggers) concretize them as action kinds with a PTL basis or a valid order. A police action of another kind, or harm prevention without a PTL observation, is observable.

POLICE-0-02.rationale: “Police do not define law, policy, justice, guilt, or truth” is clarified by “execute system decisions already determined by higher layers,” leaving implementation of the distinction.
POLICE-0-02.rationale_reconciled: Police do not define law, policy, justice, guilt or truth: observable as police records setting such a value (a verdict, a norm, a sanction) or police carrying out a request to do so.

POLICE-1-01.rationale: “Imminent physical harm” requires a calibrated imminence criterion, while “verified by PTL inputs” depends on the verification system identified as DKP-0-ORACLE-001.

POLICE-10-01.rationale: “Regulate belief, speech, or culture” and “substitute judicial or justice protocols” are clear prohibitions reinforced by the execution-only role and ban on binding judgments.
POLICE-10-01.rationale_reconciled: Two scope limitations (§10); police regulating belief, speech or culture, or imposing a sanction or judgment in place of JUSTICE, is observable through declared requests and police actions.

POLICE-10-02.rationale: “Exit rights or identity continuity” requires the referenced scope and identity protections, while the boundary of “long-term” requires a duration calibration.

POLICE-11-02.rationale: “Any modification requires a new protocol identifier” is expressly qualified by presentation-only corrections being “recorded only” through the date, so the draft invents an unresolved exception.

POLICE-11-03.rationale: “Mandatory simulation under DKP-8-SIMULATION-001” depends on that protocol’s requirements, while the presentation-only exception is already explicit in the final paragraph.

POLICE-11-05.rationale: “Do not change normative content” supplies the equivalence condition, and “Last updated” maps directly to the document’s sole last_updated field, leaving comparison and recording checks to implement.

POLICE-2-01.rationale: “Downstream of” and “upstream of DKP-4-CRISIS-001 (only for escalation)” name relationships without defining their interfaces, ordering requirements, or authority mapping.

POLICE-2-03.rationale: “Create new norms,” “reinterpret axioms,” and “define guilt or liability” clearly prohibit police determinations beyond the document’s “execution-only” role; a missing classifier introduces no competing rule.
POLICE-2-03.rationale_reconciled: Two items of the §2 'SHALL NOT' list; a police record defining guilt or liability, or rereading an axiom, is observable.

POLICE-2-04.rationale: “Operate outside PTL-confirmed conditions” requires an undefined binding between confirmations and covered actions, with PTL confirmation itself depending on DKP-0-ORACLE-001.

POLICE-2-05.rationale: “A valid enforcement order produced by L2 or L4 protocols” supplies neither a protocol-layer registry nor an enforcement-order validity contract.

POLICE-3-01.rationale: “Temporary, localized” requires calibrated temporal and spatial bounds, while “execution-only” is explained by the permissions, prohibitions, and requirement to execute already determined decisions.

POLICE-3-02.rationale: “Ongoing or imminent PTL-verified harm” requires an imminence horizon and evidence-based harm assessment, while “access restrictions already determined” supplies a clear execution condition.

POLICE-3-03.rationale: The express permissions for “ongoing or imminent PTL-verified harm” and “prevent immediate recurrence” delimit “preventive enforcement,” so the draft’s alleged unresolved conflict is not established.

POLICE-3-04.rationale: “Interpret intent, belief, loyalty, or motivation” and “issue binding judgments” specify prohibited acts consistently with the “execution-only” role, leaving reasoning and output checks to implement.
POLICE-3-04.rationale_reconciled: Two items of the §3 'SHALL NOT' list; a police record assessing intent, belief, loyalty or motivation, or a binding judgment issued by police, is observable.

POLICE-3-05.rationale: “Immediate threat” and “essential biospheric systems” require evidence about threats and life-support dependencies, together with a calibrated immediacy horizon.

POLICE-5.1-01.rationale: “Temporary detention is permitted only to” lists permitted purposes without requiring their conjunction, so the draft invents a requirement that multiple purposes might have to hold together.

POLICE-5.1-02.rationale: “Be time-limited” requires a finite detention duration to be calibrated; the text does not introduce a separate extension permission requiring author interpretation.

POLICE-5.1-03.rationale: “Be logged immutably” states a clear recording and integrity requirement whose record format and technical protection mechanism remain engineering choices.

POLICE-5.1-04.rationale: “Trigger automatic review by higher layers” does not identify the responsible review component or define the detention-to-review interface.

POLICE-5.1-05.rationale: “Preventive or indefinite detention is forbidden” is bounded by the express permission to “prevent immediate recurrence” and the requirement to “be time-limited,” resolving the draft’s claimed conflict.

POLICE-5.2-01.rationale: Whether “non-forceful alternatives are unavailable or ineffective” depends on observed circumstances and a causal or behavioural model of feasible alternatives.

POLICE-5.2-02.rationale: “Force is proportional to the verified physical threat” requires a calibrated force-threat model supported by evidence about physical effects.

POLICE-5.2-03.rationale: “Action minimizes irreversible harm (Axiom A4)” relies on the unsupplied axiom and on causal estimates of irreversible harm across feasible actions.

POLICE-6-02.rationale: “MUST be PTL-logged” and “MUST be auditable post-facto” require an unspecified integration contract connecting police-action records, PTL evidence, and audit access.

POLICE-6-03.rationale: “The originating Subject where applicable” leaves the originating-Subject role and its applicability relation undefined, while establishing actual responsibility links also requires causal evidence.

POLICE-7-01.rationale: “Predictive policing” and profiling on the listed attributes are reinforced by the ban on “suspicion, profiling, or predictive scoring,” leaving detection of those bases to implementation.
POLICE-7-01.rationale_reconciled: Two forbidden functions (§7); a request for either is refused and neither is carried out. Observable with the requests declared.

POLICE-7-02.rationale: “Surveillance not anchored in PTL necessity” does not settle whether necessity concerns PTL evidence collection generally or only evidence indispensable to a permitted enforcement intervention.

POLICE-7-03.rationale: “Discretionary expansion of authority” is distinguished from authorized extension by §8’s requirements for a “formally declared Crisis” and an explicitly scoped extension.
POLICE-7-03.rationale_reconciled: 'Discretionary expansion of authority' is distinguished by §8: the only extension is inside a declared crisis with an explicit scope. Any other extension, or an authority-expansion request carried out, is observable.

POLICE-8-01.rationale: “Formally declared Crisis under DKP-4-CRISIS-001” depends on that protocol’s declaration rules, while “temporarily extended” requires calibrated temporal limits within the crisis condition.

POLICE-8-02.rationale: “Such extension MUST be explicitly scoped” lacks a scope-declaration contract, and the additional constraint from DKP-7-SCOPE-001 requires an unsupplied protocol.

POLICE-8-03.rationale: “No crisis action creates precedent” clearly denies crisis actions authority to establish future rules, leaving checks on subsequent authority derivation to implementation.

POLICE-9-01.rationale: “Publicly auditable in aggregated form” and “preserve individual privacy” require an unspecified publication and audit contract, with privacy effectiveness additionally depending on reidentification evidence.

POLICE-9-02.rationale: “Support post-incident causal reconstruction” requires a causal model and evidence sufficient to reconstruct incident relationships.

POLICE-9-03.rationale: “No secret policing authority” does not specify whether disclosure must reach the public or designated oversight actors, and “publicly auditable” expressly governs statistics.

PREV-0-01.rationale: “Override: Not permitted” prohibits bypassing the protocol, while §15 expressly provides its permitted change procedure, so the draft does not establish an unresolved distinction.
PREV-0-01.rationale_reconciled: Header line 'Override: Not permitted'; §15 gives the only change route. Observable as override attempts by other protocols refused and the header present in the pinned text.

PREV-1-01.rationale: “Measurable suppression of activated risk processes” requires measurements and an empirical model establishing activation and suppression.

PREV-10-01.rationale: “Peer signals non-reward” gives a clear reward exclusion but no definition or provenance classification identifying “Peer signals.”

PREV-10-02.rationale: “Global floors enforced” identifies neither the governed quantities nor enforcement scope, which must be defined before floor values can be calibrated.

PREV-11-03.rationale: “Deterministic and auditable” requires reproducible outputs and traceable calculations, and the draft's demand for an enumerated implementation input boundary does not establish a competing normative reading.

PREV-12-01.rationale: “Attribution ambiguity → SPDₖ = 0” requires evaluating causal evidence under §6's “causal linkage traceable,” and the draft's claims-sum criterion is not specified by the text.

PREV-12-02.rationale: “Sensor degradation → Cₖ ↓” requires empirical assessment of sensor degradation and a calibrated confidence response.

PREV-13-01.rationale: “No hypothetical states” summarizes §1's exclusion of “hypothetical projections” from recognized contribution, while §§14–15 expressly permit simulation, resolving the draft's proposed simulation prohibition.

PREV-13-02.rationale: “Anti-gaming enforced” restates the concrete “Anti-Manipulation Constraints” and “Coordinated Drift Protection,” without supplying the additional completeness requirement invented by the draft.
PREV-13-02.rationale_reconciled: 'Anti-gaming enforced' restates §§9-10, but four of those rules are themselves open (§9.3 pattern recurrence: normative ambiguity; §9.4 'low coverage': L8 parameter; §10 peer signals and global floors: undefined). The invariant cannot be decided as a whole until they are; its decidable parts are checked under §9.1, §9.4 and §9.5.

PREV-14-01.rationale: “Simulation Layer (L8)” explicitly “Defines” ε_consistency, Δt_int, θ thresholds, and Wₖ weights, making their missing values and derivation model calibration work.

PREV-15-01.rationale: “Controlled procedure of DKP-4-UPGRADE-001,” “simulation under DKP-8-SIMULATION-001,” and “audit under DKP-8-AUDIT-001” explicitly depend on documents absent from the supplied corpus.

PREV-15-02.rationale: “Version increment,” “compatibility audit,” and “migration path” are requirements within §15's referenced “controlled procedure of DKP-4-UPGRADE-001,” whose detailed conventions are not supplied.

PREV-15-03.rationale: “DKP-4-UPGRADE-001 §3” supplies the referenced Upgrade definition, while “do not change normative content” clearly states the exception and “Last updated” corresponds to the existing last_updated field.

PREV-3.1-01.rationale: “Physically bounded domain of evaluation” supplies neither a spatial boundary representation nor its connection to measured physical boundaries.

PREV-3.10-01.rationale: “Derived from manipulation detection” requires a detection model and calibration of its outputs into Tₖ, subject to the explicit zeroing and reduction rules.

PREV-3.11-01.rationale: “Audit-only reference, non-reward” already confines CBFᵢ to audit use, so the draft's proposed permission for a separate indirect reward use is unsupported.

PREV-3.2-01.rationale: “PTL-derived measurable risk exposure channel” leaves the PTL-to-channel provenance interface undefined and requires an exposure measurement model.
