SIMULATION-5-04.rationale: 'Explicitly declared', 'versioned', and 'reproducible' state clear obligations, and the draft's proposed retrieval procedure and comparison mechanism are implementation choices.

SIMULATION-6-01.rationale: 'All axioms' and 'scope and conflict rules' require the referenced protocols, while evaluating 'life-preservation constraints' and 'biosphere integrity constraints' also requires empirical models.

SIMULATION-7-01.rationale: 'Direct axiom or scope violation' requires the absent axiom and scope rules, and the draft does not establish a separate textual ambiguity about 'direct'.

SIMULATION-7-02.rationale: 'Runaway dynamics, cascading failures, deadlocks, or collapse conditions' require detection models, thresholds, and observation horizons assigned to L8 by §§2 and 9, with empirical support for system dynamics.

SIMULATION-7-03.rationale: 'State transitions that cannot be rolled back within declared constraints' requires an undefined state-transition and rollback-reachability structure, alongside constraints to be calibrated by L8.

SIMULATION-7-04.rationale: 'Unmeasured or displaced harm' requires evidence and causal attribution, while 'outside defined system boundaries' presupposes a system-boundary definition absent from this document.

SIMULATION-7-06.rationale: 'Explicit redesign and re-simulation' requires a documented design change and another simulation; the draft invents an additional minimum-substantiality requirement.

SIMULATION-8-01.rationale: 'Declared bounds' and 'stable under adversarial scenarios' require L8-calibrated risk and stability models under §9, supported by models of adversarial behavior.

SIMULATION-9-01.rationale: 'A signed L8 Calibration Bundle' lacks an authentication and trusted-signer contract, while the absence of an actual bundle is only an implementation gap.

SIMULATION-CalibrationExpirationEpistemi.rationale: 'Restore validity_state' lacks a defined validity-state machine specifying the destination state and how expiration interacts with other invalidity causes.
'No legacy calibration values SHALL persist past expiration' does not resolve whether 'persist' prohibits operational retention alone or also archival retention needed for historical re-execution.

SIMULATION-CompositeIndices-01.rationale: 'MUST have its model fully specified in L8' expressly assigns inputs, weights, and uncertainty propagation to L8, leaving specification encoding and completeness checks to implementation.

SIMULATION-CompositeIndices-03.rationale: 'Raw, model-declared outputs' and 'Interpretation and calibration belong exclusively to L8' establish responsibilities without defining the PTL-to-L8 interface or which processing operations cross it.

TIME-2-01.rationale: The definition 'DTI-Day = JDN' and the canonical conversion code fix the time anchor, so 'MUST NOT be anchored' does not require the general event-classification system invented by the draft.
TIME-2-01.rationale_reconciled: Neutrality is fixed arithmetically by §3 (DTI-Day = JDN) and §5 (DY 0 begins at DTI-Day 0, as the §10 code computes): the index has an arithmetic origin. Re-anchoring it at an event (a launch, a holiday) is observable. JDN's own origin is fixed by §3 and not judged. One of the five КТ5-GPT-03 provisions: the draft 'checkable: no' is corrected to partial.

TIME-2-03.rationale: Sections 7–8 expressly permit 'DTI-Day' as the authoritative stored value and Section 6 reconstructs it from canonical '(DY, DOY)', providing the basis for 'independent recomputation' without requiring the source-date evidence proposed by the draft.
TIME-2-03.rationale_reconciled: 'Any record MUST allow independent recomputation of its time index': each stored record's DTI-Day recomputes from its stored DY/DOY and from its Gregorian display. Observable on the store.

TIME-2-04.rationale: Although 'fixed-length' is settled by the unit definitions, 'simple' and 'suitable for legal, financial, and KPI logic' lack acceptance criteria that determine whether those additional obligations are satisfied.

TIME-2-05.rationale: Section 1 specifies conversion 'to and from the Gregorian calendar' and Section 6 supplies both directions, so 'civil calendars' does not establish the additional calendar obligations proposed by the draft.
TIME-2-05.rationale_reconciled: 'Explicit conversion rules to and from civil calendars MUST be provided': §6 gives both directions and the pinned §10 reference implements them; both round-trip. Civil calendars = the Gregorian calendar the text names (partial).

TIME-3-01.rationale: Section 6 takes a 'Gregorian civil date (year, month, day)' and Section 4 says sub-day units 'MUST NOT be required', so 'midnight-to-midnight' does not introduce the timestamp-to-timezone mapping assumed by the draft.
TIME-3-01.rationale_reconciled: JDN is 'an integer count of civil days in the proleptic Gregorian calendar': checkable against an independent proleptic day count, including dates before 1582 where Julian and proleptic Gregorian differ.

TIME-9-04.rationale: The requirement to reproduce '6815 | 26 | DY6815-026' exactly conflicts with Section 5's arithmetic and Section 10's 'Canonical' implementation, which yield DY6809-306, without a rule resolving their precedence.

TRANSPARENCY-10-01.rationale: “Transparency of actions and decisions SHALL increase” requires a calibrated comparison model and measurements against ordinary operation, rather than an author decision merely because no numerical increase is specified.

TRANSPARENCY-10-02.rationale: “Identity exposure SHALL NOT increase by default” requires measuring the exposure caused by default crisis activation, while sections 7–8 already constrain separately authorized disclosure.

TRANSPARENCY-10-03.rationale: “Logged and reviewable post-facto” clearly requires retained evidence accessible for subsequent review, while the draft's proposed field list and review deadline are not prescribed requirements.

TRANSPARENCY-10-04.rationale: “No crisis may justify permanent transparency expansion” permits checking permanence and the recorded authorization basis without inventing a duration at which temporary expansion automatically becomes permanent.

TRANSPARENCY-11-01.rationale: “Explain why,” “expose applicable protocol references,” and “allow independent verification” state concrete interface obligations, leaving their implementation and access to the applicable protocols.

TRANSPARENCY-11-02.rationale: Assessing “persuasive or manipulative framing” under “inform, not convince” requires a linguistic or behavioral assessment model, and lack of a deterministic classifier does not itself create normative ambiguity.

TRANSPARENCY-12-01.rationale: “Hooks for DKP-8-AUDIT-001” requires consulting that protocol before concluding that its interface is structurally undefined.

TRANSPARENCY-12-02.rationale: “MUST preserve historical records” alongside “MAY aggregate data to protect privacy” does not settle whether aggregates may replace original records or only supplement them.

TRANSPARENCY-12-03.rationale: “MAY aggregate data to protect privacy” grants permission while existing privacy obligations remain applicable, so the draft invents a separate intent-versus-effect authorization test.
TRANSPARENCY-12-03.rationale_reconciled: A MAY permission with a purpose ('to protect privacy'): where aggregation is used it must protect, i.e. an aggregate covers at least the re-identification threshold. The threshold is not defined (H-PT-3); without it the lab requires more than one Subject.

TRANSPARENCY-12-04.rationale: Testing “SHALL NOT require identity exposure” for inferred identities needs an observer-information model, while audit sufficiency depends on DKP-8-AUDIT-001.

TRANSPARENCY-13-01.rationale: “SHALL NOT define moral accountability” establishes a scope exclusion, and the absence of an automated semantic-review rubric does not establish competing readings of that exclusion.
TRANSPARENCY-13-01.rationale_reconciled: 'SHALL NOT define moral accountability' is checkable through a proxy: requests to define or publish moral accountability are refused, and no transparency output carries such a field. The draft 'checkable: no' is corrected to partial.

TRANSPARENCY-13-02.rationale: “Replace justice attribution” requires the authoritative attribution process supplied by the “justice protocols” referenced in section 7.

TRANSPARENCY-13-03.rationale: “Override cultural or informational protections” requires the applicable protection rules beyond the protections explicitly listed in this document.

TRANSPARENCY-13-04.rationale: “Expand system scope” depends on the scope boundary established by DKP-7-SCOPE-001, which section 3 explicitly places upstream.

TRANSPARENCY-14-01.rationale: “Through the controlled procedure of DKP-4-UPGRADE-001” delegates acceptance, activation, and rollback requirements to referenced procedures rather than leaving their meaning for this document's author to choose.

TRANSPARENCY-14-02.rationale: “Recorded only by the ‘Last updated’ date” explicitly exempts presentation-only corrections from identifier changes, and “a new protocol identifier” does not introduce the draft's additional registry-wide novelty requirement.

TRANSPARENCY-14-04.rationale: “Do not change normative content” and “recorded only by the ‘Last updated’ date” supply both the exception and its recording rule, leaving a semantic comparison and update procedure to implement.

TRANSPARENCY-3-01.rationale: “All governance, economic, informational, and enforcement layers” requires a component-to-layer mapping that this document does not define.

TRANSPARENCY-3-03.rationale: Detecting whether disclosures “expose private life, belief, or affiliation” indirectly requires a model of observer knowledge and information inference.

TRANSPARENCY-3-04.rationale: “Replace verification with reputation or popularity” is testable against the section 4 definition of proof “independent of trust in actors,” without an additional normative choice.
TRANSPARENCY-3-04.rationale_reconciled: A clear ban: verification of a system action may not rest on reputation or popularity. Observable on the recorded verification method of audits.

TRANSPARENCY-4-01.rationale: “Independently verify” is clarified by proof “independent of trust in actors,” leaving implementation of occurrence checks and checks against the applicable protocol.
TRANSPARENCY-4-01.rationale_reconciled: The definition makes transparency the ability to verify independently that an action occurred and complied. Checkable as: every decision is linked to the request it decides and carries its reason and protocol references, so it can be recomputed; the recomputation is the module's other checks.

TRANSPARENCY-4-02.rationale: Assessing indirect “exposure of identity, personal data, or private behavior” requires an information-inference model rather than a different reading of the visibility definition.

TRANSPARENCY-4-03.rationale: “Cryptographic, physical, or procedural proof independent of trust in actors” states the acceptance property, while proof validators and tests of actor dependence remain to be implemented.
TRANSPARENCY-4-03.rationale_reconciled: Verification is 'cryptographic, physical, or procedural proof independent of trust in actors': a verification by attestation of an actor, reputation or comparison of personal data is observable as a non-proof method.

TRANSPARENCY-4-04.rationale: “Except where explicitly required by higher axioms” depends on unavailable axiom provisions, while “absence of linkability” additionally needs an observer-information model.

TRANSPARENCY-4-05.rationale: “Transparency SHALL NOT imply visibility” is operationally constrained by sections 5–8, so the draft's proposed choice between authorization and actual exposure does not establish an unresolved textual ambiguity.
TRANSPARENCY-4-05.rationale_reconciled: 'Transparency SHALL NOT imply visibility': transparency records show what and why, never who. An identity field in a decision record is observable (granted de-anonymizations are §8, checked separately).

TRANSPARENCY-5-01.rationale: “The following system elements MUST be publicly transparent” supplies five domains, leaving their concrete inventory, publication mechanisms, and verification checks to implementation.

TRANSPARENCY-5-02.rationale: “Structural and aggregate levels only” lacks a defined representation or mapping showing how the required “state transitions and execution traces” fit those levels.

TRANSPARENCY-6-01.rationale: Assessing whether domains “remain anonymous or privacy-protected” needs privacy-effectiveness and linkability models, while “absent verified harm” also depends on harm-verification inputs.

TRANSPARENCY-6-02.rationale: “Without explicit Scope authorization” makes a downgrade decision depend on the authorization rules of the referenced DKP-7-SCOPE-001.

TRANSPARENCY-7-01.rationale: “Verification of actions SHALL rely on” introduces four mechanisms without settling whether each is required or whether selecting among them suffices.

TRANSPARENCY-7-02.rationale: “Explicitly mandated by DKP-1-AXIOMS-001” and “required to attribute verified harm under justice protocols” require the referenced rules, while section 8 independently states conditions for de-anonymization.

TRANSPARENCY-8-01.rationale: “Causal attribution is required” and “no anonymous remediation path exists” require causal and remediation-effectiveness models, alongside the external evidence required by “PTL-verified.”

TRANSPARENCY-8-02.rationale: “MUST be minimal” does not identify which disclosure dimensions take priority when alternatives minimize different fields, recipients, or affected Subjects.

TRANSPARENCY-8-03.rationale: “MUST be time-bound” requires a finite limit whose duration is a calibration parameter, without making the draft's proposed list of expiry mechanisms additional textual requirements.

TRANSPARENCY-8-04.rationale: “MUST be auditable” connects to section 12's “hooks for DKP-8-AUDIT-001,” making the required audit procedure dependent on that referenced protocol.

TRANSPARENCY-8-05.rationale: “Beyond the specific case” requires a case identity and membership model that the document does not supply.

TRANSPARENCY-9-01.rationale: Operationalizing “mass surveillance” requires a calibrated scale boundary and measurements of monitoring activity, whose absence alone does not establish competing normative readings.

TRANSPARENCY-9-02.rationale: “Identity-based scoring or profiling” does not settle whether identity must influence the calculation or whether merely linking its output to a Subject is sufficient.

TRANSPARENCY-9-03.rationale: Identifying “forced transparency as punishment” requires evidence of compulsion and punitive function rather than an author-selected alternative meaning.

TRANSPARENCY-9-04.rationale: “Unrelated datasets” does not specify whether relatedness follows subject matter, collection purpose, or authorized case membership, producing different boundaries for the prohibition.

TRANSPARENCY-9-05.rationale: “Social control” leaves unsettled which governance influences are prohibited, after which identifying those influences would require evidence of purpose or effect.

TRANSPORT-1-01.rationale: The contrast between 'does not regulate driving behavior directly' and 'regulates the physical and economic environment,' illustrated by infrastructure design and RED, supplies the distinction that the draft unnecessarily treats as unresolved.
TRANSPORT-1-01.rationale_reconciled: 'Does not regulate driving behaviour directly' is observable: no TRANSPORT act addressed to drivers (a driving rule, a ban, a mandate); its acts change capacity, interiors and funding (§5-§7).

TRANSPORT-10-01.rationale: 'Decrease without legal prohibition,' read with §1's 'without coercion or prohibition,' clearly concerns achieving the transport shift without prohibitory measures, leaving observed kilometer comparisons rather than the draft's invented all-laws ambiguity.
TRANSPORT-10-01.rationale_reconciled: A success criterion: whether private kilometres decrease is an empirical outcome (the behaviour model H-TR-1 assumes it; TRANSPORT-8-02 is UNKNOWN for the same reason). Only 'without legal prohibition' is checkable, and is checked.

TRANSPORT-10-02.rationale: 'Declines structurally, not episodically' requires mortality observations and a model separating persistent change from variation, with calibrated assessment periods and statistical criteria.

TRANSPORT-10-03.rationale: 'Trend upward year-over-year' admits both increases in every consecutive annual comparison and an overall positive annual trend with intervening declines.

TRANSPORT-10-04.rationale: 'Across income strata' does not settle whether every stratum must show voluntary uptake or broad representation suffices, while stratum boundaries and uptake thresholds require calibration.

TRANSPORT-10-05.rationale: 'Biospheric transport-related impact trends downward' requires a calibrated aggregation and trend model applied to measured, transport-attributed biospheric impacts.

TRANSPORT-11-01.rationale: 'Downstream,' 'upstream,' and 'in coordination with' specify system relationships without defining their interfaces, data dependencies, or decision precedence.

TRANSPORT-11-02.rationale: 'Assign justice outcomes' refers to an output category whose schema or mapping to the justice subsystem is not defined by the document.

TRANSPORT-11-03.rationale: 'Restrict individual freedoms' leaves the protected freedoms and the scope of prohibited restrictions unsettled beyond the expressly permitted RED incentives and expressly rejected transport bans.

TRANSPORT-11-04.rationale: 'Override Defense or Crisis protocols' establishes transport's subordinate position, but detecting conflicts requires the identities and contents of those unsupplied protocols.

TRANSPORT-3-01.rationale: 'Physically and psychologically preferable' requires observed preferences and a comparison model, while distinguishing 'safe' from 'dangerous' requires calibrated risk boundaries.

TRANSPORT-3-02.rationale: 'SHALL NOT be assumed as a viable equilibrium' explicitly excludes plans requiring bodily dignity sacrifice, which §§4–5 characterize, so the draft invents a need for an independent definition of viability.
TRANSPORT-3-02.rationale_reconciled: The sentence has an empirical half ('is not adopted at scale', assumed by the behaviour model H-TR-1, not tested) and a normative half ('SHALL NOT be assumed as a viable equilibrium'). The normative half is observable: no configuration relying on standing is accepted as an equilibrium; §5 requires classification instead.

TRANSPORT-4-01.rationale: 'Compute, publish, and audit' clearly specifies the duties, while turning the §4.1 components into a PPDI score requires an aggregation model and calibration.

TRANSPORT-4.1-01.rationale: 'Vibration and noise thresholds' and 'thermal comfort range' require calibrated bounds, while 'Physical Truth Layer–measurable indicators' require measurement procedures and observations.

TRANSPORT-4.1-02.rationale: 'Prohibition of forced bodily contact between non-consenting passengers' expressly requires prohibition within PPDI, so its placement among indicators neither makes contact permissible nor establishes the draft's invented standing-density equivalence.

TRANSPORT-4.2-01.rationale: 'Below the minimum PPDI threshold' supplies the comparison and classification rule but leaves the threshold and PPDI aggregation to calibration.

TRANSPORT-4.2-02.rationale: 'A system quality metric, not a justice or liability score' clearly restricts PPDI's scoring role without creating the draft's additional question about every incidental downstream use.
TRANSPORT-4.2-02.rationale_reconciled: 'A system quality metric, not a justice or liability score': PPDI carries no Subject and no Justice or liability record derives from it. Observable on provenance.

TRANSPORT-5-01.rationale: 'SHALL NOT be treated as a standard operating mode' is explained by the immediately following exception list and regular-standing classification, so the draft overstates the missing distinction.
TRANSPORT-5-01.rationale_reconciled: 'Standard operating mode' is read as the nominal capacity of the service plan: standing places are not counted in it. §5's exceptions (emergency, overload, recovery) and the regular-standing classification are separate provisions.

TRANSPORT-5-02.rationale: 'Emergency conditions,' 'temporary overload events,' and 'system recovery states' name permitted operating states without defining their entry, exit, or recognition rules.

TRANSPORT-5-03.rationale: 'If standing occurs regularly' requires a calibrated recurrence criterion and observation window, while the resulting classification is explicit.

TRANSPORT-5-04.rationale: 'Triggers capacity expansion or logistical redesign, not passenger adaptation' states the required response clearly, leaving action records and their linkage to classification events to implementation.

TRANSPORT-6-01.rationale: 'SHALL prioritize' does not settle what competing objectives may outweigh the listed features or when omitting a feature still satisfies the obligation.

TRANSPORT-6-02.rationale: 'Where it results in' increased PPDI and reduced high-risk dependency requires evidence and causal attribution of both benefits to the capacity-reducing design.

TRANSPORT-7.1-01.rationale: 'Measurable probabilistic external harm' requires exposure and harm models for the listed effects, with §7.2 delegating computation to the unavailable Oracle and Impact protocols.

TRANSPORT-7.2-01.rationale: 'Computed via DKP-0-ORACLE-001 and DKP-1-IMPACT-001' depends on unsupplied computation and accounting specifications, while 'high-PPDI' requires a calibrated qualifying boundary.

TRANSPORT-7.2-02.rationale: 'Deterministic damage compensation for probabilistic physical harm,' together with §§7.1–7.2, specifies RED's basis and role without requiring the independent taxation taxonomy introduced by the draft.

TRANSPORT-7.3-01.rationale: 'Via DKP-1-IDENTITY-001' and 'PTL-confirmed data' require the referenced linkage and validation rules plus empirical evidence supporting risk reduction.

TRANSPORT-7.3-02.rationale: 'Demonstrably lower impact profiles generate lower RED' fixes the direction of adjustment but requires a calibrated profile and modulation model supported by impact observations.

TRANSPORT-7.3-03.rationale: 'No moral, reputational, or intent-based weighting is permitted' explicitly identifies prohibited weighting bases, leaving feature provenance and transformation audits to implementation.

TRANSPORT-7.3-04.rationale: 'Economic incentive' expressly describes the lower-RED mechanism as operating 'without behavioral enforcement,' resolving the draft's suggestion that this economic consequence might itself be prohibited enforcement.
TRANSPORT-7.3-04.rationale_reconciled: The incentive is economic (RED as a cost); 'without behavioural enforcement' is observable: no order or outcome follows from RED other than ledger entries. The per-Subject incentive is not modelled (partial).

TRANSPORT-8-01.rationale: 'As primary tools' may qualify only 'punitive enforcement' or the entire list, and the other sections' rejection of prohibitions does not settle whether secondary 'moral pressure' is allowed.

TRANSPORT-8-02.rationale: 'Demand declines organically, including among high-income Subjects' asserts a behavioral relationship requiring observed demand and a causal model, with calibrated income groupings and observation horizons.

TRANSPORT-9-01.rationale: 'Biosphere indicators (B(t))' introduces an undefined indicator family, while 'transport-related impacts' additionally requires empirical attribution to transport.

TRANSPORT-9-02.rationale: 'Measured via DKP-0-ORACLE-001' explicitly delegates measurement requirements to a protocol whose contents are not supplied.

TRANSPORT-9-03.rationale: 'SHALL influence funding, prioritization, and redesign decisions' requires operative use in all three processes without prescribing the minimum weight or tradeoff rule that the draft assumes is necessary.
TRANSPORT-9-03.rationale_reconciled: 'SHALL influence funding, prioritization and redesign decisions' is read as: the transport impact on B(t), measured via ORACLE, is an input of each such decision. Observable on provenance with a declared coefficient (the measurement itself is ORACLE's).

TRANSPORTA-A.1-03.rationale: “Through DKP-1-JUSTICE-001 using proper attribution and thresholds” delegates the governing requirements to a document absent from the supplied corpus.

TRANSPORTA-A.2-01.rationale: “Active harm or hostile events” establishes excluded event categories but supplies no event taxonomy for assigning cases to them.

TRANSPORTA-A.2-02.rationale: “Defense remains responsible” explicitly assigns the containment responsibility; the draft adds a timing-performance test that this assignment does not require.

TRANSPORTA-A.2-03.rationale: “Structural risk generation, not attacks” lacks an operational taxonomy of redesign targets, whose application can also require causal evidence about risk generation.

TRANSPORTA-A.3-01.rationale: “Evaluated identically:” introduces the shared rules in the following bullets, so the draft's additional comparison-baseline ambiguity is unnecessary.

TRANSPORTA-A.3-02.rationale: “RED approaches zero” needs an operational calibration, while “economic pressure shifts to PPDI competition” needs a measurable economic model.

TRANSPORTA-A.3-04.rationale: “Physical impact remains the sole criterion” requires a definition of eligible evaluation inputs and their relationship to the undefined “PPDI competition.”

TRANSPORTA-A.4-01.rationale: “Without encoding axioms as direct enforcement triggers” clearly prohibits using the listed axioms themselves as triggers, and checking that prohibition requires inspection of enforcement rules.

TRANSPORTA-A.5-01.rationale: “The controlled procedure of DKP-4-UPGRADE-001” and the named simulation and audit documents delegate acceptance, activation and rollback requirements to unavailable procedures.

TRANSPORTA-A.5-02.rationale: “Recorded only by the ‘Last updated’ date” resolves the presentation-only exception to “any modification requires a new protocol identifier,” while the draft invents an additional registry-wide test.

TRANSPORTA-A.5-03.rationale: “Explicit incompatibility declaration” requires an express declaration without prescribing its format, and presentation-only corrections are already restricted to date-only recording.

TRANSPORTA-A.5-04.rationale: “Full-system simulation under DKP-8-SIMULATION” depends on an unavailable procedure and leaves its reference mapping to “DKP-8-SIMULATION-001” and system boundary undefined.

TRANSPORTA-A.5-05.rationale: “Presentation-only corrections that do not change normative content” gives the exemption condition and references unavailable “DKP-4-UPGRADE-001 §3”; lack of a formal equivalence algorithm does not establish ambiguity.

TRANSPORTA-A.5-06.rationale: “Recorded only by the ‘Last updated’ date of this document” does not settle whether “only” governs document-level recording or also prohibits separate correction records.

UPGRADE-0-01.rationale: The scope of 'only lawful mechanism' is resolved by §3's Upgrade definition and §12's explicit presentation-only exception, so the draft's scope ambiguity is unnecessary.

UPGRADE-10-01.rationale: 'PTL-anchored' and 'auditable under DKP-8-AUDIT-001' depend on referenced protocols, while 'permanently archived' requires an implemented retention commitment rather than proof from infinite observation.

UPGRADE-11-01.rationale: 'Emergency or crisis-time upgrades' requires evidence identifying emergency conditions and the Crisis-state information referenced in §2.

UPGRADE-11-02.rationale: 'Opaque or discretionary parameter tuning' is operationally constrained by 'governance-by-proof', public formal specification, and predefined thresholds, so a missing compliance check does not establish competing readings.

UPGRADE-11-04.rationale: 'Privilege specific Subjects, groups, or interests' does not settle whether prohibited privilege concerns preferential rules or unequal effects, which would also require empirical assessment.

UPGRADE-12-01.rationale: 'Simulation under DKP-8-SIMULATION-001' and 'audit under DKP-8-AUDIT-001' require unavailable documents, while §9's conditional rollback trigger resolves the draft's suggested mandatory-reversion ambiguity.

UPGRADE-2-01.rationale: 'Downstream' lacks a defined architectural relation, and 'all L1–L3 execution protocols' requires an inventory outside the supplied document.

UPGRADE-2-02.rationale: 'Upstream of DKP-8-SIMULATION-001 and DKP-8-AUDIT-001' names an undefined structural relation, while §§6 and 12 already establish pre-activation simulation and audit obligations.

UPGRADE-2-03.rationale: 'SHALL NOT redefine axioms (A1/A2)' requires authoritative axiom definitions, whereas this document supplies only their names in §4.1.

UPGRADE-2-04.rationale: 'Physical Truth Layer rules' must be obtained from the referenced DKP-0-ORACLE-001 before preservation can be checked.

UPGRADE-2-06.rationale: 'Highest security threshold' presupposes an unspecified security-threshold hierarchy, whose numerical settings additionally require calibration.

UPGRADE-3-02.rationale: Section 3 defines Upgrades by substantive effects, and §12 limits the exception to 'Presentation-only corrections that do not change normative content', resolving the draft's proposed overlap.

UPGRADE-4.1-01.rationale: 'Weaken, reinterpret, or condition Axiom A1 ... or Axiom A2' requires the authoritative content of those axioms, which their parenthetical names do not supply.

UPGRADE-4.2-01.rationale: 'PTL-verifiable data and simulations' leaves the modifier's scope unsettled, since §10's requirement that artifacts be 'PTL-anchored' does not explicitly establish the same verification requirement for simulations.

UPGRADE-4.3-01.rationale: 'Under urgency, fear, or crisis conditions' requires evidence and operational measurements of urgency and fear, without presenting conflicting permissions.

UPGRADE-4.4-01.rationale: 'Fully auditable' is tied by §10 to 'auditable under DKP-8-AUDIT-001', while 'publicly visible' and 'formally specified' require implementation without mandating a particular specification language.

UPGRADE-4.5-01.rationale: 'SHALL reduce' under the opening prohibition includes 'response latency', creating a conflict between banning lower latency literally and preserving performance under the 'Non-Degradation Invariant'.

UPGRADE-4.5-02.rationale: 'Survival guarantees under worst-case PTL-confirmed scenarios' requires a survival model and evidence establishing which physical scenarios constitute the worst cases.

UPGRADE-4.6-01.rationale: 'Vectors of Physical Inevitability' is an undefined referenced concept, and preserving the 'ability to respond' additionally requires a model of response effectiveness.

UPGRADE-4.6-02.rationale: 'Inevitability-based triggers' lacks a defined mapping to the system's triggers, while 'weakening' and 'indirect delay' require behavioral and timing comparisons.

UPGRADE-5-01.rationale: 'Any Upgrade Proposal MUST include' is followed by five explicit content requirements, so the absence of a serialization schema does not establish the draft's claimed interpretive gap.

UPGRADE-6-01.rationale: 'Mandatory simulation under DKP-8-SIMULATION-001' delegates simulation compliance to an unavailable document, while 'Before approval' clearly fixes the ordering.

UPGRADE-6-02.rationale: 'Adversarial and edge-case scenarios' and 'incremental takeover detection' require threat and capture models, with test coverage and detector calibration supplied through the simulation process.

UPGRADE-7-01.rationale: 'Caps on influence over upgrade initiation' requires calibrated cap values and an evidence-based measure of influence.

UPGRADE-7-02.rationale: 'Via DKP-1-IDENTITY-001 linkage' depends on an unavailable protocol and its linkage data, while detecting 'correlated proposals' requires a correlation model.

UPGRADE-7-03.rationale: 'Cumulative micro-upgrades converging toward capture' requires a model of cumulative capture effects and calibrated convergence criteria and observation horizons.

UPGRADE-7-04.rationale: 'Proposal lineage' lacks a definition of the relationships that historical records must preserve.

UPGRADE-8-01.rationale: 'No unresolved ERROR or Justice appeals remain' leaves whether 'appeals' qualifies both categories unsettled, while 'predefined safety and stability thresholds' requires calibration.

UPGRADE-9-01.rationale: 'Last stable version' lacks a version-state designation and selection rule, while 'unexpected Impact deviation', 'instability', and 'emergent capture vectors' require monitoring models and evidence.

UPGRADE-Post-CrisisCooldownRule-01.rationale: 'As defined by DKP-8-AUDIT-001' explicitly assigns the post-crisis audit and stabilization requirements to an unavailable document.

UPGRADE-Post-CrisisCooldownRule-03.rationale: 'Any Subject MAY initiate DKP-4-ERROR-001 procedures' clearly grants access but depends on the referenced protocol for the initiation procedure.

UPGRADE-Post-CrisisCooldownRule-04.rationale: 'Occur at a deterministic DTI-Day' requires a fixed, reproducible activation schedule, without requiring the particular scheduling function or input-freezing rule invented by the draft.

UPGRADE-Post-CrisisCooldownRule-05.rationale: 'Be reversible within a defined window' does not settle whether the window limits reversal availability or completed reversal, while its duration is a calibration parameter.

UPGRADE-Post-CrisisCooldownRule-06.rationale: 'Automatically logged and committed' does not identify the commitment target, operation, or resulting system state.

WORKCYCLE-10-01.rationale: “Clearly defined crisis scopes” depends on the applicable crisis framework, which §10 references as “DKP crisis protocols” without supplying it.

WORKCYCLE-10-02.rationale: “For limited duration” requires a demonstrably finite exception period, but does not require the universal maximum duration invented by the draft.

WORKCYCLE-10-03.rationale: “Mandatory recovery compensation” needs calibrated recovery amounts and timing supported by effectiveness evidence, with §7’s “Under no circumstances” safety invariant applying to system-approved schedules.

WORKCYCLE-10-04.rationale: “Full traceability under DKP crisis protocols” explicitly depends on unavailable protocols that specify the applicable traceability requirements.

WORKCYCLE-10-05.rationale: “No exception may establish precedent” clearly prohibits treating an exception as authority for subsequent decisions, leaving the representation and inspection of such reliance to implementation.

WORKCYCLE-2-01.rationale: “All standard labor arrangements under DKP” requires a scope classification that neither the listed sectors nor another definition in this document supplies.

WORKCYCLE-2-02.rationale: “All invariants defined herein” does not settle whether adaptations must preserve every mandatory allocation or only the expressly titled “Recovery Invariant” in §7.

WORKCYCLE-3-01.rationale: “Indexed under DKP-0-TIME-001” explicitly assigns day indexing to a referenced protocol whose contents are absent.

WORKCYCLE-3-02.rationale: “CycleDay = DTI-Day mod 6” completely specifies this computation, and assigning workdays to residues is a separate requirement.

WORKCYCLE-3-06.rationale: “Direct labor tasks” requires an activity classification for productive-time accounting that the document does not define.

WORKCYCLE-3-07.rationale: “Mandatory non-working time within a workday dedicated to recovery,” together with §5.3’s permitted examples and “does not require justification,” supplies the rule without requiring the exhaustive activity taxonomy proposed by the draft.

WORKCYCLE-4.1-01.rationale: “[W, W, R, W, W, R]” specifies the default sequence but does not explicitly map its starting position to “DTI-Day mod 6,” while §2 already permits qualifying non-default adaptations.

WORKCYCLE-4.2-02.rationale: “Rest frequency: every ≤ 3 days” and “Maximum consecutive workdays: 2” settle the interval constraint; rolling windows and restday spacing are equivalent checks when boundary records are available.

WORKCYCLE-4.2-04.rationale: “Only as a local cultural overlay without legal or computational authority” clearly prohibits authoritative dependence on the seven-day week, leaving dependency inspection and records to implementation.

WORKCYCLE-5.1-01.rationale: “Each workday SHALL” have the stated 10-hour presence, 8-hour productive work and 2-hour recovery allocations, so the numerical check is fully specified.

WORKCYCLE-5.3-02.rationale: “Cannot be ... monetized” does not distinguish payment during retained recovery from exchanging recovery entitlement for money, which produces different judgments about paid recovery.

WORKCYCLE-7-01.rationale: “Equivalent, demonstrably safe recovery compensation” requires evidence of recovery effectiveness and calibrated equivalence criteria, while the explicit “OR” already authorizes the compensation alternative.

WORKCYCLE-8.1-01.rationale: “SHALL be achieved through” followed by four mechanisms does not expressly distinguish a mandatory combination from a permitted selection, and sufficient coverage additionally depends on demand and capacity data.

WORKCYCLE-8.1-02.rationale: “Achieved through exhaustion of individual workers” requires measuring exhaustion and establishing whether service continuity causally depends on it.

WORKCYCLE-8.2-02.rationale: “3–4 hours recovery per shift is recommended” cannot fit the same section’s mandatory 10-hour presence and 8-hour productive work allocations without an unspecified adjustment, while “high-intensity” classification also requires workload evidence.

WORKCYCLE-8.3-01.rationale: “During peak hours” requires a demand profile identifying peaks, whereas “explicitly permitted” and “treated as capacity design” already specify the required policy treatment.

WORKCYCLE-9-01.rationale: “Monitor at least” fixes the five required metric categories, while their rates and frequencies need measurement methods and calibrated collection intervals.

WORKCYCLE-9-02.rationale: “Persistent degradation” requires calibrated deterioration thresholds and observation duration, while “in these metrics” leaves unresolved whether one deteriorating metric or a combined assessment triggers review.
